paragraphs: Rabbi Yose of Pekiin died. Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Shimon heard a raven chirping and understood that there was no one to attend to him. He, Rabbi Abba, and his companions went. He had a little son of five, who would let no one attend to his father. He wept over him, mouth upon mouth: ‘Master of the world, it is written, “You shall surely send away the mother, but the children you may take.” Take me and my sister!’ Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Abba wept at the child’s voice. A pillar of fire separated them, and a heavenly voice came forth: ‘The child’s tears have ascended before the throne. Thirteen people have been given on your account, and they have added twenty-two years for you to learn with the child.’ Rabbi Yose opened his eyes. Rabbi Yose said that after thirteen years he would reveal what he had seen in that world. Through the 370 tears—another version, 305—which my little son shed, three hundred thousand benches of the heavenly academy trembled, and all sought mercy for me. Zohar, Balak, at the locator עשע״ח; see there at great length.
